patch.value: Refusal recovery bundles echo URL credentials verbatim: attempted_command and normalized_args repeat a credentialed package source on stdout and in logs

Found 2026-11-08 during the CodeRabbit review of PR 1688. redactSensitiveCommandArgs (src/sdk/command-line.ts) redacts only history redact invocations. Every other refusal copies the raw argv into recovery.attempted_command and recovery.normalized_args, so a package source carrying URL credentials is repeated verbatim in the structured error on stdout, in CI logs and in any agent transcript. Reproduced with the built CLI and a fake credential. 'pm package install https://u:fake-secret@example.invalid/x.tgz --project --dry-run --bogus-flag --json' fails with unknown_option, and its attempted_command contains u:fake-secret. 'pm package --catalog --install <same> --output-limit 2' fails with read_output_mutation_conflict and shows the same echo. PR 1688 already withholds that refusal's executable retry for such an argv (pm-rrwh2o), so its recovery adds no further copy; the general echo predates that change. Telemetry already strips URL userinfo through stripUrlCredentials and redactUrlsInText in src/core/telemetry/policy.ts, but the CLI recovery path does not use them. Duplicate check: searched recovery attempted_command credentials url secret redact package source; pm-m0fh (closed) covered tracked files, not runtime refusal output.

Every CLI recovery representation (attempted_command, normalized_args, provided_fields, suggested_retry and suggested_retry_args) removes URL userinfo from every token, or withholds an executable retry when removing it would change the command's meaning; a spec drives an unknown_option refusal and a read_output_mutation_conflict refusal with a credentialed package source and asserts that no secret appears in stdout or stderr; history redact keeps its existing flag-value redaction
Refusal recovery output names a credentialed package source without its userinfo, and no secret appears in stdout or stderr
attempted_command and normalized_args repeat https://u:fake-secret@example.invalid/x.tgz verbatim for unknown_option and read_output_mutation_conflict refusals

value.text: Scope note from the PR 1688 Codex review: removing userinfo must cover every spelling the URL parser normalizes, not only the literal '//user:secret@'. A backslash authority behind a wrapper, such as npm:https:\user:secret@host, parses to the same credentials. pm-rrwh2o's carriesUrlCredentials, which parses each URL-scheme suffix with new URL, is the detection this item can reuse for redaction.
